paragraphs: Northwest Bancshares, Inc., a Maryland corporation, was incorporated in 2009 to be the successor corporation to Northwest Bancorp, Inc., the former stock holding company for Northwest Bank, upon completion of the mutual-to-stock conversion of Northwest Bancorp, MHC. The terms "Northwest", "the Company", "we", "us" and "our" refer to Northwest Bancshares, Inc., unless indicated otherwise by the context.

The conversion was completed in 2009 when the Company sold 68,878,267 shares of common stock at $10.00 per share in the related offering. Concurrent with the completion of the offering, shares of Northwest Bancorp, Inc. common stock owned by public stockholders were exchanged for shares of Northwest Bancshares, Inc.'s common stock. We also issued 1,277,565 shares of common stock and contributed $1.0 million in cash from the offering proceeds to Northwest Charitable Foundation, a charitable foundation that we established for the benefit of the communities in which Northwest Bank operates. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had 146,107,964 shares outstanding and a market capitalization of approximately $1.753 billion.
Our executive offices are located at 3 Easton Oval, Suite 500, Columbus, Ohio 43219. We also maintain administrative offices located at 100 Liberty Street, Warren, Pennsylvania 16365.

The Company's website (www.northwest.com) contains a direct link to Northwest Bancshares, Inc.'s filings with the SEC, including copies of annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and amendments to these filings, if any. Information on our website shall not be considered a part of this report. Copies of our filings may be obtained, without charge, by written request to Shareholder Relations, 3 Easton Oval, Suite 500, Columbus, Ohio 43219, or emailing shareholderrelations@northwest.com.

Northwest Bank is a Pennsylvania-chartered savings bank headquartered in Warren, Pennsylvania, which is located in northwestern Pennsylvania. Northwest Bank is a community-oriented financial institution offering personal and commercial banking solutions, investment management and trust services. Northwest Bank's mutual savings bank predecessor was founded in 1896.

As of December 31, 2025, Northwest Bank operated 161 community-banking locations throughout its market area in Pennsylvania, western New York, northeastern Ohio, and Indiana. Our principal lending activities are the origination of loans secured by first
mortgages on owner-occupied, one-to-four-family residences, shorter term consumer loans, and commercial business and commercial real estate loans.

Our principal sources of funds are personal and business deposits, borrowed funds and the principal and interest payments on loans and marketable securities. Our principal source of income is interest received on loans and marketable securities. Our principal expenses are the cost of employee compensation and benefits and the interest paid on deposits and borrowed funds.
Northwest Bank's principal executive office is located at 100 Liberty Street, Warren, Pennsylvania 16365, and the telephone number at that address is (814) 726-2140.

On July 25, 2025, the Company completed its acquisition of Penns Woods Bancorp, Inc. ("Penns Woods"), pursuant to the merger agreement, which was entered into by the Company and Penns Woods on December 16, 2024 (the "Merger Agreement"). In accordance with the Merger Agreement, the Company and Penns Woods completed a business combination whereby Penns Woods merged with and into the Company (the "Merger"), with the Company as the surviving corporation in the Merger. Immediately after the effective time of the Merger (the "Effective Time"), Penns Woods' wholly-owned subsidiary banks, Luzerne Bank, a Pennsylvania-chartered state bank, and Jersey Shore State Bank, a Pennsylvania-chartered state bank, merged with and into Northwest Bank, with Northwest Bank as the surviving bank in the subsidiary bank mergers. Under the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, at the Effective Time, each share of Penns Woods' common stock, $5.55 par value, issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (except for Treasury Shares (as provided for in the Merger Agreement), converted, in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Merger Agreement, into a right to receive 2.385 shares of common stock, $0.01 par value, of the Company.

The Penns Woods results of operations are included in the Company's consolidated results since the date of acquisition. Therefore, the Company's year to date 2025 results reflect increased levels of average balances, net interest income, and noninterest expense compared to the prior year results. After purchase accounting fair value adjustments, the acquisition added $2.2 billion of total assets, including $1.8 billion of loans, $160 million of investments, of which $82 million were immediately sold, as well as $2.0 billion of total liabilities, primarily consisting of $1.6 billion in deposits. The Company recorded preliminary goodwill of $63 million and core deposit intangibles of $42 million related to the acquisition.

Northwest Bank is headquartered in northwestern Pennsylvania and has expanded primarily through acquisitions, into the southwestern and central regions of Pennsylvania, as well as western New York, northeastern Ohio, and Indiana. As of December 31, 2025, we operated 161 community banking locations across these market areas. All of the aforementioned market areas are served by a number of competing financial institutions. As a result, we encounter strong competition both in attracting deposits and in originating loans. Our most direct competition for deposits comes from other banks, brokerage houses and credit unions in our market areas. We expect continued competition from these financial institutions in the foreseeable future. With the continued acceptance of internet banking by our customers and consumers generally, competition for deposits has increased from institutions operating outside of our market area.

The following description of our market area is based upon information obtained from SNL Securities, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Federal Housing Financial Agency and the Mortgage Bankers Association.

Pennsylvania Market Area. Our retail branch network of 102 community banking offices within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania encompasses 29 counties. Our western Pennsylvania market has a diverse economy driven by healthcare and education industries, service businesses, technology companies and small manufacturing operations. Our southeastern Pennsylvania market is primarily driven by service businesses but also serves as a bedroom community to the cities of Baltimore, Maryland and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

headings: Risks Related to our Lending Activities

Our commercial loan portfolio is increasing and the inherently higher risk of loss may lead to additional provisions for credit losses or charge-offs, which would negatively impact earnings and capital.
The level of our commercial real estate loan portfolio may subject us to additional regulatory scrutiny.
If the allowance for credit losses is not sufficient to cover actual credit losses, our earnings could decrease.
The foreclosure process may adversely impact our recoveries on non-performing loans.
Risks Related to Laws and Regulations
Changes in laws and regulations and the cost of compliance with new laws and regulations may adversely affect our operations and our income.
Non-compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act, as amended, and its implementing regulations, or other laws and regulations could result in fines or sanctions.

We are subject to numerous laws designed to protect consumers, including the Community Reinvestment Act and fair lending laws, and failure to comply with these laws could lead to material penalties and other sanctions.

We could become subject to more stringent capital requirements, which could adversely impact our return on equity, require us to raise additional capital, or constrain us from paying dividends or repurchasing shares.
The Federal Reserve Board may require us to commit capital resources to support Northwest Bank.
Legal and regulatory proceedings and related matters could adversely affect us or the financial services industry in general.
Data privacy and cybersecurity are areas of heightened legislative and regulatory scrutiny.
Risks Related to Market Interest Rates
The reversal of the historically low interest rate environment has and may continue to adversely affect our net interest income and profitability.
Changes in interest rates could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
Hedging against interest rate exposure may adversely affect our earnings.
Risks Related to Economic Conditions
The monetary policies of the Federal Reserve Board could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Inflation can have an adverse impact on our business and on our customers.
We could be adversely affected by the soundness of other financial institutions and other third parties we rely on.
A lack of liquidity could adversely affect the Company's financial condition and results of operations.
Risks Related to our Business Strategy
Acquisitions may disrupt our business and dilute stockholder value.
Our continued pace of growth may require us to raise additional capital during unfavorable market conditions.
New lines of business or new products and services may subject us to additional risks.
Our business strategy includes growth, and our financial condition and results of operations could be negatively affected if we fail to grow or fail to manage our growth effectively.
Risk Related to Competitive Matters
Strong competition may limit growth and profitability.
We may be subject to intellectual property-related disputes or may fail to effectively obtain, maintain, defend, or enforce our intellectual property rights.
Risks Related to Operational Matters
Risks associated with system failures, interruptions, or cybersecurity breaches could negatively affect our earnings.
Our risk management framework may not be effective in mitigating risk and reducing the potential for significant losses.
Our board of directors relies to a large degree on management and outside consultants in overseeing cybersecurity risk management.
Our business may be adversely affected by an increasing prevalence of fraud and other financial crimes.
Risks Related to Environmental and Other Global Matters
We are subject to environmental liability risk associated with lending activities.
A slowdown in economic growth or a resumption of recessionary economic conditions due to global events could have an adverse effect on our business in the future.
paragraphs: In addition to factors discussed in the description of our business and elsewhere in this report, as well as other filings we make with the SEC, the following are factors that could adversely affect our future results of operations and financial condition.

Commercial loans generally expose a lender to greater risk of non-payment and loss than one- to four-family residential mortgage loans because repayment of the loans often depends on the successful operation of the business and the income stream of the borrowers. Such loans typically involve larger loan balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers compared to one- to

four-family residential mortgage loans. Also, many of our commercial borrowers have more than one loan outstanding with us. Consequently, an adverse development with respect to one loan or one credit relationship can expose us to a significantly greater risk of loss compared to an adverse development with respect to a one- to four-family residential mortgage loan. Commercial business loans expose us to additional risk since they typically are dependent on the borrower's ability to make repayments from the cash flows of the business and are secured by non-real estate collateral that may depreciate over time. Further, our commercial business loans may be secured by collateral other than real estate, such as inventory and accounts receivable, the value of which may be more difficult to appraise, control or collect and may be more susceptible to fluctuation in value at the time of default. In addition, if we foreclose on these loans, our holding period for the collateral may be longer than for a single or multi-family residential property if there are fewer potential purchasers of the collateral.

The FDIC and the other federal banking regulatory agencies have jointly promulgated the CRE Lending Guidance on sound risk management practices for financial institutions with concentrations in commercial real estate lending. Under the CRE Lending Guidance, a financial institution that, like us, is actively involved in commercial real estate lending should perform a risk assessment to identify concentrations. A financial institution may have a concentration in commercial real estate lending if, among other factors, (i) total reported loans for construction, land acquisition and development, and other land represent 100% or more of total capital, or (ii) total reported loans secured by multi-family and non-farm residential properties, loans for construction, land acquisition and development and other land, and loans otherwise sensitive to the general commercial real estate market, including loans to commercial real estate related entities, represent 300% or more of total capital. Based on these factors, we have a concentration in residential and commercial real estate lending, as such loans represent a combined 342% of total bank capital as of December 31, 2025. The particular focus of the guidance is on exposure to commercial real estate loans that are dependent on the cash flow from the real estate held as collateral and that are likely to be at greater risk to conditions in the commercial real estate market (as opposed to real estate collateral held as a secondary source of repayment or as an abundance of caution). The purpose of the CRE Lending Guidance is to guide banks in developing risk management practices and capital levels commensurate with the level and nature of real estate concentrations. The CRE Lending Guidance states that management should employ heightened risk management practices including board and management oversight and strategic planning, development of underwriting standards, risk assessment and monitoring through market analysis and stress testing. While we believe we have implemented policies and procedures with respect to our commercial real estate loan portfolio consistent with this guidance, bank regulators could require us to implement additional policies and procedures consistent with their interpretation of the guidance that may result in additional costs to us or that may result in a curtailment of our multi-family and commercial real estate lending that would adversely affect our loan originations and profitability. For additional information, see "Supervision and Regulation—Federal Banking Regulation—Real Estate Lending Standards and Guidance."

Our customers may not repay their loans according to the original terms, and the collateral, if any, securing the payment of these loans may be insufficient to pay any remaining loan balance. We may experience significant credit losses, which may have a material adverse effect on operating results. We make various assumptions and judgments about the collectability of the loan portfolio, including the creditworthiness of borrowers and the value of the real estate and other assets serving as collateral for the repayment of loans. If our assumptions prove to be incorrect, the allowance for credit losses may not be sufficient to cover losses inherent in our loan portfolio, resulting in additions to the allowance. Material additions to the allowance would materially decrease net income.

Our emphasis on originating commercial real estate and commercial loans is one of the more significant factors in evaluating the allowance for credit losses. As we continue to increase the amount of such loans, increased provisions for credit losses may be necessary, which would decrease our earnings. In addition, any future credit deterioration could require us to increase our allowance for credit losses in the future.

paragraphs: Our principal business consists of collecting deposits and making loans primarily secured by various types of collateral, including real estate and other assets in the markets in which we are located. Attracting and maintaining deposits is affected by a number of factors, including interest rates paid on competing deposits and other investments offered by other financial and non-financial institutions, account maturities, fee structures, and levels of personal income and savings. Lending activities are affected by the demand for funds and thus are influenced by interest rates, the number and quality of alternative lenders and regional economic conditions. Sources of funds for lending activities include deposits, borrowings, repayments on loans, cash flows from investment and mortgage-backed securities and income provided from operations.

Our earnings depend primarily on net interest income, which is the difference between interest earned on our interest-earning assets, consisting primarily of loans and investment securities, and the interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities, consisting primarily of deposits, borrowed funds, and trust-preferred securities. Net interest income is a function of our interest rate spread, which is the difference between the average yield earned on our interest-earning assets and the average rate paid on our interest-bearing liabilities, as well as a function of the average balance of interest-earning assets compared to the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities. Also contributing to our earnings is noninterest income, which consists primarily of service charges and fees on loan and deposit products and services, fees related to investment management and trust services, net gains and losses on the sale of assets, including SBA loans, and mortgage banking income. Net interest income and noninterest income are offset by provisions for credit losses, general administrative and other expenses, including employee compensation and benefits, occupancy expense and processing costs, as well as by state and federal income tax expense.

Our net income was $126 million, or $0.92 per diluted share, for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $100 million, or $0.79 per diluted share, for the year ended December 31, 2024, and $135 million, or $1.06 per diluted share, for the year ended December 31, 2023. The provision for credit losses was $56 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $25 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, and $23 million for the year ended December 31, 2023.

paragraphs: Northwest Bancshares, Inc., 一間馬裏蘭州公司，於 2009 年設立，作為 Northwest Bancorp, Inc. 的繼承公司，Northwest Bancorp, Inc. 為 Northwest Bank 的前股票持有公司，於 Northwest Bancorp, MHC 從合夥轉為股票形式後成立。文中 "Northwest"、"the Company"、"we"、"us" 及 "our" 皆指 Northwest Bancshares, Inc.，除非文意另有說明。

該轉換於2009年完成，當時本公司在相關發行中出售了68,878,267股普通股，每股價格為10.00美元。與發行完成同時，公眾股東持有的Northwest Bancorp, Inc.普通股兌換為Northwest Bancshares, Inc.普通股。我們亦發行了1,277,565股普通股，並從發行所得現金中貢獻1.0百萬美元至Northwest Charitable Foundation，這是一個我們為服務Northwest Bank營運地區社區而設立的慈善基金。截至2025年12月31日，本公司已發行146,107,964股，市值約為1.753十億美元。
本公司總部位於 3 Easton Oval, Suite 500, Columbus, Ohio 43219。本公司亦於 100 Liberty Street, Warren, Pennsylvania 16365 設有行政辦公室。

本公司網站 (www.northwest.com) 提供直接連結至本公司向 SEC 提交的檔，包括 10-K 年度報告、10-Q 季度報告、8-K 現況報告，以及這些檔的修正檔（如有）。本公司網站上的資訊不應視為本報告的一部分。本公司檔可免費索取，請以書面請求寄送至 Shareholder Relations, 3 Easton Oval, Suite 500, Columbus, Ohio 43219，或電郵至 shareholderrelations@northwest.com。
Northwest Bank 是一家在賓夕法尼亞州註冊的儲蓄銀行，總部設於賓夕法尼亞州華倫市，位於賓夕法尼亞州西北部。Northwest Bank 是一家以社區為導向的金融機構，提供個人及企業銀行服務、投資管理與信託服務。Northwest Bank 的合作夥伴儲蓄銀行前身於 1896 年成立。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Northwest Bank 在賓夕法尼亞州、西部紐約州、東北俄亥俄州及印第安納州的市場區域內運作 161 間社區銀行據點。我們的主要貸款業務為發放以第一優先權抵押品為擔保的貸款
抵押貸款用於所有權人自用、一至四戶住宅、短期消費貸款，以及商業企業及商業不動產貸款。
本公司主要資金來源為個人及企業存款、借入資金，以及貸款及可交易證券的本金與利息償還。本公司主要收入來自貸款及可交易證券的利息收入。本公司主要費用為員工薪資及福利成本，以及存款及借入資金所支付的利息。
Northwest Bank 的主要營業處所位於 100 Liberty Street, Warren, Pennsylvania 16365，該地址的電話號碼為 (814) 726-2140。

於 2025 年 7 月 25 日，本公司完成對 Penns Woods Bancorp, Inc.（"Penns Woods"）的收購，根據於 2024 年 12 月 16 日由本公司與 Penns Woods 簽訂的合併協議（"合併協議"）。根據合併協議，本公司與 Penns Woods 完成一項業務合併，使 Penns Woods 合併進本公司（"合併"），本公司為合併後的存續公司。自合併生效時間（"生效時間"）起，Penns Woods 的 wholly-owned 子銀行 Luzerne Bank，一間 Pennsylvania 簽證的州立銀行，以及 Jersey Shore State Bank，一間 Pennsylvania 簽證的州立銀行，均合併進 Northwest Bank，Northwest Bank 為子銀行合併後的存續銀行。根據合併協議的條款及條件，於生效時間，每 shares of Penns Woods 的普通股，$5.55 面值，於生效時間前發行且流通的 shares（除 Treasury Shares（如合併協議所規定）外），依合併協議所規定的程序，轉換為取得本公司普通股，$0.01 面值，2.385 shares 的權利。

自收購日開始，Penns Woods 的營運成果已納入本公司合併財務報表。因此，本公司截至 2025 年的年度營運成果，與前一年相比，平均餘額、淨利息收入及非利息費用均有增加。經購併會計公允價值調整後，該收購增加了總資產 2.2 十億美元，包括貸款 1.8 十億美元、投資 160 百萬美元，其中 82 百萬美元已立即出售，以及總負債 2.0 十億美元，主要為存款 1.6 十億美元。本公司已記錄初步商譽 63 百萬美元及核心存款無形資產 42 百萬美元，與該收購相關。

Northwest Bank 設立於西北部 Pennsylvania，主要透過收購方式擴張至 Pennsylvania 的西南部及中部地區，以及西部 New York、東北部 Ohio 及 Indiana。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司在這些市場區域經營 161 間社區銀行據點。上述所有市場區域均有許多競爭對手金融機構。因此，本公司在吸引存款及貸款發放方面均面臨強烈競爭。本公司在存款方面的最直接競爭對手為市場區域內的其他銀行、證券經紀公司及信用合作社。本公司預期在可預見的未來，這些金融機構仍將持續競爭。隨著客戶及一般消費者對網際銀行的接受度持續提高，來自市場區域外機構的存款競爭也有所增加。
以下對我們市場區域的描述係根據從 SNL Securities、勞工統計局、美國住房金融機構管理局及房貸銀行協會所取得的資訊。
Pennsylvania 市場區域。我們在 Pennsylvania 州內設有 102 間社區銀行據點，涵蓋 29 個縣。我們在西部 Pennsylvania 的市場擁有多元化的經濟，主要由醫療保健及教育產業、服務業、科技公司及小型製造業推動。我們在東南部 Pennsylvania 的市場則主要由服務業推動，同時也作為馬裏蘭州巴爾的摩市及賓夕法尼亞州費城的住宅社區。

paragraphs: 本公司主要業務為收取存款並發放貸款，貸款主要以各種類型的擔保品為抵押，包括位於我們營運地區的不動產及其他資產。吸引並維持存款受到許多因素的影響，包括競爭性存款及其它金融與非金融機構所提供的投資產品的利率、帳戶到期日、費用結構，以及個人收入與儲蓄水平。貸款業務受到資金需求的影響，因此會受到利率、替代貸款人的數量與品質以及區域總體經濟條件的影響。貸款業務的資金來源包括存款、借款、貸款償還、投資與房貸支持證券的現金流以及營運所產生的收入。

本公司獲利主要取決於淨利息收入，淨利息收入為本公司利息收入資產（主要為貸款與投資證券）所賺取的利息，與利息負債（主要為存款、借款及信託優先證券）所支付的利息之間的差額。淨利息收入取決於我們的利率差，即我們利息收入資產的平均收益率與我們利息負債的平均支付率之間的差額，以及我們利息收入資產的平均餘額與利息負債的平均餘額的比較。此外，也對我們獲利有所貢獻的是非利息收入，主要為貸款與存款產品及服務的服務費用與手續費、投資管理與信託服務相關費用、資產銷售的淨收益與損失（包括SBA貸款），以及房貸銀行收入。淨利息收入與非利息收入會被信貸損失準備金、一般行政與其他費用（包括員工薪資與福利、營運費用與處理成本），以及州與聯邦所得稅費用所抵銷。

本公司淨收入為 126 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 0.92 美元，於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年相比 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年為 100 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 0.79 美元，以及 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年為 135 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 1.06 美元。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，信貸減損提撥為 56 百萬美元，相比 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年為 25 百萬美元，以及 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年為 23 百萬美元。

headings: 與我們貸款業務相關的風險
我們的商業貸款組合正在增加，而內在較高的損失風險可能導致額外的信貸損失備抵或核銷，這將對營業收入與資本產生負面影響。
我們的商業不動產貸款組合規模可能使我們面臨額外的監管審查。
若信貸損失備抵不足以覆蓋實際信貸損失，則我們的營業收入可能會減少。
拍賣程序可能對我們在不良貸款上的回收產生負面影響。
與法律與法規相關的風險
法律與法規的變更以及遵守新法律與法規的成本，可能對我們的營運與收入產生負面影響。
未遵守銀行保密法（Bank Secrecy Act）及其實施法規，或其他法律與法規，可能會導致處以罰款或制裁。
本公司受多項法律規範，旨在保護消費者，包括社區再投資法案及公平貸款法規，未能遵守這些法律規範可能會導致重大處罰及其他制裁。
本公司可能面臨更嚴格的資本要求，這可能會對本公司權益回報率產生不利影響，或要求本公司籌措額外資本，或限制本公司發放紅利或回購股票。
美國聯邦儲備委員會可能要求本公司投入資本資源以支援西北銀行。
法律及監管程序及相關事項可能會對本公司或整個金融服務業產生不利影響。
資料隱私權及網路安全是目前立法及監管機構高度關注的領域。
與市場利率相關的風險
歷史性低利率環境的逆轉已並可能繼續對本公司淨利息收入及獲利能力產生不利影響。
利率變動可能會對本公司營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
對抗利率風險的對沖措施可能會不利影響我們的獲利。
與總體經濟條件相關的風險
美國聯邦儲備理事會的貨幣政策可能會不利影響我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果。
通貨膨脹可能對我們的業務及我們的客戶產生不利影響。
我們可能因其他金融機構的健全性及其他我們所倚賴的第三方的狀況而受到不利影響。
流動性不足可能會不利影響本公司的財務狀況及營運成果。
與本公司業務策略相關的風險
併購可能會干擾我們的業務並稀釋股東價值。
我們持續的成長速度可能需要在不利的市場環境下籌集額外資金。
新業務線或新產品與服務可能使我們面臨額外風險。
我們的業務策略包含成長，若我們未能成長或未能有效管理成長，將可能對我們的財務狀況及營運結果產生負面影響。
與競爭相關的風險
強烈的競爭可能限制成長與獲利能力。
我們可能面臨智慧財產權相關爭議，或可能無法有效取得、維持、辯護或執行我們的智慧財產權權利。
與營運相關的風險
與系統故障、中斷或網路安全事件相關的風險可能對我們的營收產生負面影響。
本公司風險管理架構可能無法有效降低風險並減少重大損失之潛在可能性。
本公司董事會在監督資安風險管理方面，很大程度依賴管理階層及外部顧問。
本公司業務可能因詐欺及其他財務犯罪事件日益普遍而受到不利影響。
與環境及其他全球議題相關之風險
本公司因貸款業務而面臨環境責任風險。
因全球事件導致經濟成長減緩或復甦至衰退經濟條件，可能對本公司未來業務產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 除本報告中於業務說明部分及其他地方所討論的影響因素，以及我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交的其他申報文件中所列的因素外，以下因素可能對我們未來的營運結果與財務狀況產生不利影響。

商業貸款通常使貸款人面臨較一至四戶住宅抵押貸款更高的無法償還與損失風險，因為貸款的償還往往取決於借款人業務的運作成效及其收入來源。此類貸款通常對單一借款人或相關借款人集團的貸款金額較一至四戶住宅抵押貸款為高。此外，我們許多商業借款人可能同時持有數筆貸款。因此，針對某一筆貸款或某一信用關係的不利發展，可能使我們面臨較一至四戶住宅抵押貸款更高的損失風險。商業營運貸款使我們面臨額外風險，因為這些貸款通常取決於借款人從業務現金流中償還貸款的能力，且以非不動產擔保品為抵押，而這些擔保品可能隨時間而 depreciate。此外，我們的商業營運貸款可能以除不動產以外的擔保品為抵押，例如存貨與應收帳款，其價值可能較難評估、控制或回收，且在違約時其價值可能更容易出現波動。另外，若我們對這些貸款進行拍賣，則擔保品的持有時間可能長於單一或多戶住宅不動產，若擔保品的潛在買家較少的話。

In addition, if we foreclose on these loans, our holding period for the collateral may be longer than for a single or multi-family residential property if there are fewer potential purchasers of the collateral.

美國聯邦存款保險公司及其它聯邦銀行監管機構共同頒佈了 CRE 貸款指引，用以規範金融機構在商業不動產貸款集中度方面的健全風險管理作法。根據 CRE 貸款指引，像我們這樣積極參與商業不動產貸款的金融機構，應進行風險評估以識別集中度。金融機構可能因下列因素之一而具有商業不動產貸款集中度：(i) 建築貸款、土地取得及開發貸款及其他土地貸款總計佔總資本 100% 或以上，或 (ii) 以多戶住宅及非農業住宅不動產為擔保的貸款、建築貸款、土地取得及開發貸款及其他土地貸款，以及其它可能受總體經濟商業不動產市場條件影響的貸款，包括對商業不動產相關機構的貸款，總計佔總資本 300% 或以上。根據這些因素，我們在住宅及商業不動產貸款方面具有集中度，因為這些貸款總計佔總銀行資本的 342% ，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。指引特別關注的是對依賴不動產擔保物現金流的商業不動產貸款的風險，這些貸款可能因總體經濟商業不動產市場條件而面臨較高風險（與作為次要償還來源或作為預防措施的不動產擔保物不同）。CRE 貸款指引的目的是引導銀行建立與不動產集中度的性質和程度相符的風險管理作法及資本水平。CRE 貸款指引指出，管理層應採用加強的風險管理作法，包括董事會及管理層的監督與戰略規劃、制定貸款標準、風險評估與監測，透過市場分析及壓力測試進行。雖然我們認為已針對商業不動產貸款組合實施與此指引相符的政策與程序，但銀行監管機構可能要求我們實施與其對指引的解釋相符的額外政策與程序，這可能會導致我們產生額外成本，或可能導致我們縮減多戶住宅及商業不動產貸款業務，進而對我們的貸款發放及獲利造成不利影響。如需更多資訊，請參閱 "監管與規範—聯邦銀行監管—不動產貸款標準與指引。"

我們的客戶可能無法依照原始條件償還貸款，且用以擔保貸款償還的抵押品可能不足以償還任何剩餘貸款餘額。我們可能面臨重大信用損失，這可能對營運結果產生重大不利影響。我們對貸款組合的可收回性做出各種假設與判斷，包括借款人的信用worthiness及用以償還貸款的不動產及其他資產的價值。如果我們的假設證明錯誤，則信用損失準備金可能不足以覆蓋貸款組閤中內在的損失，導致信用損失準備金增加。信用損失準備金的重大增加將對淨收入產生重大不利影響。
我們對商業不動產及商業貸款的強調是評估信用損失準備金時最重要的因素之一。隨著我們持續增加這類貸款的金額，可能需要增加信用損失準備金，這將降低我們的獲利。此外，任何未來的信用惡化都可能導致我們未來必須增加信用損失準備金。
